source_name: QuantumBPM (quantumbpm.com - BPMN/DMN engine vendor: blog, docs, product pages)
enumeration_method: The site is small enough to read in full, so the population is closed and every item was opened. Start: the site's own sitemap.xml, which lists 84 URLs. It omits the blog's taxonomy and author routes, so the population was closed by diffing the union of every in-page link against the sitemap: 10 tag pages (/blog/tags/<tag>), the tag index (/blog/tags), the archive (/blog/archive), two author pages (/blog/authors/rbizik, /blog/authors/jkristof) and two docs category pages (/docs/category/legal, /docs/category/projects) were found that way and are enumerated as items, as is the blog pagination route (/blog/page/2, which the sitemap does list). Re-running the diff leaves it empty: the only non-population internal links are the downloadable process files (/assets/files/support-agent.bpmn and support-agent-routing.dmn), which are link targets of an enumerated page, judged with it and captured in the corpus (record 001). No keyword facet was used to narrow the population. The one platform facet was checked afterwards, unfiltered: the blog's own tag page /blog/tags/agents ("2 posts tagged with 'AI Agents'") names exactly the two posts this census found to discuss AI in their own body, so the facet set and the census set coincide and no AI artefact sits outside the facet.
note: 100/100 URLs fetched over plain HTTPS (all HTTP 200; no login, captcha, paywall or rate limit, so no BLOCKED row). Evidence channels, and how complete each is. (1) Downloadable BPMN/DMN files - complete: the whole site offers exactly three inventory-wide (support-agent.bpmn and support-agent-routing.dmn on the anchor post, linked twice from it); both were downloaded and parsed element by element and are the decisive evidence for record 001. (2) BPMN 2.0 XML inside the page - complete: 10 pages publish BPMN XML excerpts in code blocks (blog/saga-pattern-bpmn, docs/bpmn/compensation, docs/bpmn/messaging, docs/bpmn/variables and the six docs/bpmn/elements/* reference pages); every block was extracted and searched for an agent/AI task type and none contains one. The match is strict (a bpmn:/quantum: prefix or the BPMN spec URI) because loose matching false-positives on task_type in Prometheus metrics and on DMN's own <definitions> element. (3) Figure inventory - complete by name and alt text: 61 distinct non-chrome figures across the population, each listed with its alt text and page; exactly two pages carry an AI token in any figure name or alt (blog/how-bpmn-engines-work, blog/orchestrating-ai-agents-with-bpmn) and those are the two records. (4) Full page text - complete for all 100 items, with the article body separated from the site chrome. That separation is this source's one methodological trap and it decides which exclusions may be called mechanical: the site chrome (sidebar "Recent posts", footer) repeats post titles such as "Orchestrating AI Agents with BPMN" on every page of the site, so a whole-page AI/LLM keyword test flags all 100 items. The mechanical E2 test is therefore applied to the page's own <article> body; under that test 12 pages carry a BPMN artefact with no AI/LLM token in the body. Recorded limitation, tooling not source: this session could not render images - opening a downloaded PNG returned no viewable content - so no figure was inspected by eye. Judgements rest on alt text, file names, XML and prose, and the records whose claim is "an AI element is drawn inside the process" carry needs_visual_check: true. Residual risk: an AI element drawn inside a figure whose page never names AI in text, alt or filename. No such page exists by any other channel, but the reviewer should confirm the two recorded figures (both captured at native size, 1578x458 and 1720x462) and the landing-page hero (record 003). No item was excluded for being marketing, small, simple, non-English or similar to another; the E1 rows each name the non-BPMN notation they reject (a plain-text arrow chain; five ASCII box-and-arrow sketches: deployment pipeline, job dispatch loop, DMN versioning, enterprise deployment architecture, OIDC token flow).

source_name: QuantumBPM (quantumbpm.com - BPMN/DMN engine vendor: blog, docs, product pages)
enumeration_method: The site is small enough to read in full, so the population is closed and every item was opened. Start: the site's own sitemap.xml, which lists 84 URLs. It omits the blog's taxonomy and author routes, so the population was closed by diffing the union of every in-page link against the sitemap: 10 tag pages (/blog/tags/<tag>), the tag index (/blog/tags), the archive (/blog/archive), two author pages (/blog/authors/rbizik, /blog/authors/jkristof) and two docs category pages (/docs/category/legal, /docs/category/projects) were found that way and are enumerated as items, as is the blog pagination route (/blog/page/2, which the sitemap does list). Re-running the diff leaves it empty: the only non-population internal links are the downloadable process files (/assets/files/support-agent.bpmn and support-agent-routing.dmn), which are link targets of an enumerated page, judged with it and captured in the corpus (record 001). No keyword facet was used to narrow the population. The one platform facet was checked afterwards, unfiltered: the blog's own tag page /blog/tags/agents ("2 posts tagged with 'AI Agents'") names exactly the two posts this census found to discuss AI in their own body, so the facet set and the census set coincide and no AI artefact sits outside the facet.
note: 100/100 URLs fetched over plain HTTPS (all HTTP 200; no login, captcha, paywall or rate limit, so no BLOCKED row). Evidence channels, and how complete each is. (1) Downloadable BPMN/DMN files - complete: the whole site offers exactly three inventory-wide (support-agent.bpmn and support-agent-routing.dmn on the anchor post, linked twice from it); both were downloaded and parsed element by element and are the decisive evidence for record 001. (2) BPMN 2.0 XML inside the page - complete: 10 pages publish BPMN XML excerpts in code blocks (blog/saga-pattern-bpmn, docs/bpmn/compensation, docs/bpmn/messaging, docs/bpmn/variables and the six docs/bpmn/elements/* reference pages); every block was extracted and searched for an agent/AI task type and none contains one. The match is strict (a bpmn:/quantum: prefix or the BPMN spec URI) because loose matching false-positives on task_type in Prometheus metrics and on DMN's own <definitions> element. (3) Figure inventory - complete by name and alt text: 61 distinct non-chrome figures across the population, each listed with its alt text and page; exactly two pages carry an AI token in any figure name or alt (blog/how-bpmn-engines-work, blog/orchestrating-ai-agents-with-bpmn) and those are the two records. (4) Full page text - complete for all 100 items, with the article body separated from the site chrome. That separation is this source's one methodological trap and it decides which exclusions may be called mechanical: the site chrome (sidebar "Recent posts", footer) repeats post titles such as "Orchestrating AI Agents with BPMN" on every page of the site, so a whole-page AI/LLM keyword test flags all 100 items. The mechanical E2 test is therefore applied to the page's own <article> body; under that test 12 pages carry a BPMN artefact with no AI/LLM token in the body. Recorded limitation, tooling not source: this session could not render images - opening a downloaded PNG returned no viewable content - so no figure was inspected by eye. Judgements rest on alt text, file names, XML and prose, and the records whose claim is "an AI element is drawn inside the process" carry needs_visual_check: true. Residual risk: an AI element drawn inside a figure whose page never names AI in text, alt or filename. No such page exists by any other channel, but the reviewer should confirm the two recorded figures (both captured at native size, 1578x458 and 1720x462) and the landing-page hero (record 003). No item was excluded for being marketing, small, simple, non-English or similar to another; the E1 rows each name the non-BPMN notation they reject (a plain-text arrow chain; five ASCII box-and-arrow sketches: deployment pipeline, job dispatch loop, DMN versioning, enterprise deployment architecture, OIDC token flow). Update 2026-09-25: the two needs_visual_check flags of this ledger and the UNCERTAIN verdict of the landing-page row (n=1) are superseded. The orchestrator ran the visual checks this session could not (visual check by orchestrator elicitation-5a, 2026-09-25): the two AI figures of blog/how-bpmn-engines-work are legible BPMN diagrams whose AI steps are service tasks, and the landing-page hero is a BPMN holiday-booking saga with compensation boundary events and no AI element, so n=1 is now EXCLUDE E2-no-ai-element and its captures are in ledgers/quantumbpm.raw/ rather than corpus/quantumbpm/. The counts in the footer are the standing ones: the record 003 mentioned above was withdrawn.
